title: Hosted API embeddings + rerank demo
summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of Hosted API focusing on embeddings + rerank for Lumatech's search relevance use case. Walkthrough included API calls, Console routing, Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization, and discussion on latency/cost tradeoffs and security (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Agreed next steps: send pricing + security pack, run a 2-week hosted pilot with sample corpus, schedule performance benchmark with their dataset.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-29
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE); Marco Diaz (Redwood SE); Evan Chen (Lumatech Head of Search); Priya Rao (Lumatech SRE); Tom Gill (Lumatech Data Scientist)

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Aisha from Redwood, with Marco our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Evan: Good thanks, excited to see this. We sent over a brief doc about our search issues, hope you saw it.
[00:12] Aisha: Yep, saw it — ranking drift on recent content and some latency spikes when we do re-ranking, right?
[00:18] Tom: Yeah, exactly. We run a two-stage search: vector recall then a reranker. The reranker is getting costly and sometimes hurts P99.
[00:28] Marco: Cool, that's exactly what we wanted to demo — Hosted API embeddings plus our reranking endpoint and Console tools and Optimize recommendations for cost/latency. Quick agenda: qualification, API walkthrough, Console live demo, Optimize tips, Q&A, next steps.
[00:40] Priya: Sounds good. We care about data residency and KMS integration — we are SOC 2 in progress.
[00:46] Aisha: Noted.

[01:05] Marco: Alright jumping in. First, embeddings endpoint. Example request: POST /v1/embeddings with model redwood-embed-2, payload has text array. We return vectors and metadata. (slight pause) In the Console you can see usage and token-level cost breakdown.
[01:30] Tom: Quick Q: what's the dimension on that model?
[01:33] Marco: 1024 dims by default for that model, and we have smaller footprint variants. Also we do automated normalize steps.

[02:10] Marco: For reranking we have a rerank endpoint which accepts query + candidate docs as embeddings or raw text. We internally run a cross-attention step that reorders candidates. You can either send precomputed embeddings or let us compute them at request time.
[02:40] Evan: If we already store vectors in our DB, better to send embeddings. Saves time.
[02:44] Marco: Exactly. In the demo I'll show both flows.

[03:15] [Screen share starts] Marco: Ok I'm in the Console now, going to show a sample re-rank call. Here's Playgrounds -> API Explorer.
[03:30] Marco: Example call: POST /v1/rerank body { query: "...", candidates: [...], model: "redwood-rerank-1" } returns scores + order. We also return per-candidate logits and a confidence score.
[04:00] Priya: Are those logits raw or calibrated?
[04:03] Marco: They're raw but we provide a calibrated score field when you opt-in in the request. Not super heavy compute, but helpful for thresholds.

[04:25] Marco: Now switching to Optimize suggestions — for your workload from the doc we recommend: batch size ~64 for embeddings ingest, prefix KV cache for frequent queries, and quantized model variant (int8) for rerank to save cost while retaining accuracy.
[04:48] Tom: Do you have benchmarks for int8 vs fp16 on our type of queries?
[04:51] Marco: We do — I'll share a short spreadsheet. On average int8 gives 2.3x cost reduction with ~1-2% quality delta on rerank for similar-length candidates. (murmur) But we always recommend running evals on your test set.

[05:30] Evan: What about latency? Our P99 needs to be under 250ms for rerank stage.
[05:35] Marco: For hosted API, typical P95 for rerank with int8 is ~120-180ms for 10 candidates; P99 can stretch depending on cold KV states. We have routing + hot KV to reduce that. For strict SLOs Dedicated is an option.
[05:55] Priya: If we go hosted, how do you handle data retention and logs? We need 7 years of audit logs in our system for compliance.
[06:05] Aisha: We can provide audit logs exports and long-term retention as an add-on, and we integrate with customer KMS for encryption-at-rest. We also support VPC peering and private endpoints for network isolation.

[06:30] Tom: Any concerns about hallucination or reranker producing unstable results?
[06:35] Marco: Reranker is deterministic given inputs; main variance comes from upstream embeddings or model updates. We provide eval tooling to track regressions per prompt set and automated rollback.

[07:00] Evan: Walk me through pricing for these endpoints roughly.
[07:03] Aisha: For hosted: embeddings per 1k vectors pricing tiered; rerank priced per call (compute units) and we show cost per request in the Console. I'll send a pricing sheet after.

[07:30] Marco: Demoing an actual request now — sending a query and 20 candidates as embeddings. (typing) Response back in 160ms, scores look reasonable.
[07:48] Tom: Nice. Any rate limits? We have bursts during peak indexing.
[07:52] Aisha: We have quotas and burst capacity; you can apply for higher burst limits or move to Dedicated for guaranteed throughput.

[08:20] Marco: Sharing some design notes — smart routing can route low-cost queries to cheaper model variants and high-priority queries to low-latency routes. Also caching: we support prefix caching for repeated queries and KV cache to reuse generation state for long sessions.
[08:50] Priya: Can we bring our own keys?
[08:53] Aisha: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we integrate with KMS and can set up a managed key with restricted access.

[09:20] Evan: Security — are you SOC 2 and ISO?
[09:23] Aisha: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 — yes. We'll attach our attestation in the follow-up.

[09:40] Tom: For routing and canary rollouts, does Console support A/B tests between rerank models?
[09:45] Marco: Yes, our Rollouts feature does canary/A-B with automatic fallback. You can route by user segment, percent traffic, or latency. Console shows comparative metrics.

[10:15] Marco: Now quick look at logs — here's token-level cost per call. you can filter by route/model and export CSV.

[10:40] Evan: Ok so for our next step we'd want a short pilot: run embeddings for 200k docs and test rerank on nightly traffic for 2 weeks. Can you commit to a POC that includes support from SE to tune batching?
[10:50] Aisha: Yes, SE-led POC is typical. We'll provide an onboarding doc, an eval harness and a checklist.

[11:10] Priya: We also have procurement items: standard terms and our DPA — legal will be involved.
[11:15] Aisha: We'll share our standard contract and DPA and can redline.

[11:35] Marco: Couple of technical notes: if you store embeddings in your Vector DB (e.g., Pinecone), we can integrate via connectors and you still use our reranker. Also watch out for embedding normalization mismatches across systems.

[12:05] Tom: Any limitations on candidate size? We sometimes rerank long documents.
[12:10] Marco: Rerank supports candidate text up to ~8k tokens in the hosted variant; for longer docs we recommend chunking or using a summary-first approach.

[12:45] Evan: For SLOs, if we want strict p99 guarantees we should explore Dedicated?
[12:50] Marco: Correct — Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput with SLA-backed uptime/latency. Hosted is best if you want faster time-to-value.

[13:20] Marco: Slight note — earlier in the doc we saw "K V cash" in the auto-transcript lol — the transcriber mangled KV cache.
[13:28] (laughter)

[13:45] Aisha: Alright wrapping up: recap — we demoed embeddings + rerank, Console insights, Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization, and answered security questions.
[13:55] Evan: Nice. Next steps?
[14:00] Aisha: We'll send: 1) Pricing sheet 2) SOC2/ISO and security pack + DPA 3) SE POC checklist 4) short spreadsheet with int8 vs fp16 benchmark and an eval harness. We'll also propose dates for a 2-week pilot starting the week of Oct 11.
[14:20] Tom: Sounds good. Can Marco run a quick benchmark on our sample 5k queries?
[14:25] Marco: Yes, please share the sample via S3 link and we'll run it and share results within 5 business days.

[14:40] Priya: Legal will ask for vendor security questionnaire, is that ok?
[14:44] Aisha: Absolutely, we'll fill it out, expect initial draft in 3 business days.

[15:05] Aisha: Anything else?
[15:10] Evan: That's it for now, thanks.
[15:12] Aisha: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack and schedule.

[15:30] (meeting ends)

Note: transcript has occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache, "samel" for SAML).
